Russian Attacks Force Closure of 2 Major Kyiv Bridges, Metro Line — Russian attacks have forced the closure of Kyiv’s North and South bridges, suspended part of the Green Line metro and rerouted public transport. The strikes are part of a series of attacks on the capital’s river crossings since October.

Ukraine Hits Major Russian Petrochemical Hub — Ukrainian drones targeted Russia’s Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat petrochemical complex in Bashkortostan, reportedly sparking a major fire, as attacks were also reported on the Crimean Bridge and an electrical substation in Kursk. Moscow claimed its air defenses intercepted 1,441 Ukrainian drones overnight, including around 800 reportedly heading toward the capital.

Crimean Bridge Arch Collapses Into Sea After Fresh Ukrainian Missile Strike — Ukraine reportedly struck the Crimean Bridge with four cruise missiles overnight Nov. 16-17, causing a major road arch to collapse into the water, according to Ukrainian monitoring channels and Russian milbloggers.

Trump Pivots on Ukraine as Moscow Blocks Europe — President Donald Trump says he will discuss Ukraine with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping at Thursday’s summit in China, reversing earlier White House guidance. Meanwhile, European leaders are preparing a parallel summit in Berlin focused on Ukraine’s security guarantees and defense funding, as Moscow continues resisting Europe’s participation in peace negotiations.

IMF Reports Major Progress in Ukraine Talks, Bringing $1.6 Billion in Aid Closer — The IMF reported significant progress in talks with Ukraine on the second and third reviews of its $8.1 billion loan program. Successful completion could unlock $1.6 billion, although further agreements and board approval are required.

Russian Aircraft Violate Japanese Airspace, Triggering Fighter Jet Scramble — Japan scrambled fighter jets after two suspected Russian aircraft violated its airspace Tuesday, Nov. 17, prompting a diplomatic protest. South Korea also deployed fighter jets after Russian military aircraft entered its air defense identification zone.

Woman Pulled Alive From Rubble After Russian Strike on Zaporizhzhia — Ukrainian rescuers freed a 51-year-old woman trapped beneath rubble after a Russian strike on an industrial facility in Zaporizhzhia. Separate Russian drone attacks killed a driver and injured another woman.

N. Korea Sends Russia Dozens of Missiles Monthly: Zelensky — President Zelensky says Russia receives dozens of North Korean ballistic missiles monthly and is expanding domestic missile production. Meanwhile, the Kremlin says Putin could meet Kim Jong Un at this week’s APEC summit in China.

Russian Missiles Hit 2 Major Kyiv Bridges, Damage Critical Infrastructure — Russian missiles struck Kyiv’s North and South bridges late Monday, Nov. 16, damaging critical infrastructure and disrupting essential services. Three people were injured in the Cherkasy region as Russia launched attacks across Ukraine.

California Governor Newsom Visits Ukraine — California Governor Gavin Newsom announced new medical aid for Ukraine during a visit to Lviv on Sunday, Nov. 15, which includes a 50-bed field medical station, more than 1,300 hospital beds, over 11 million bandages and 20 generators. Newsom, who is reportedly weighing a 2028 presidential bid, visited Lychakiv Cemetery, a rehabilitation center, and defense tech companies. The visit comes less than two weeks after Democrats won both chambers of Congres

72 Dead in Russian Strike as Komyshuvakha Search Ends — Search and rescue operations concluded in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region on Monday, Nov. 16, two weeks after Russian forces launched guided-bombs on a humanitarian aid site. According to Ukraine’s National Police, the death toll climbed to 72, with four people remaining missing. Russia shelled the village 11 times during the search, injuring police officers and rescuers. Regional Governor Mykhailo Semikin called it the deadliest attack i

ASELSAN Neutralizes 51 Drones Simultaneously — Turkish defense company ASELSAN said its EJDERHA AD 200 (Dragon) High Power Electromagnetic (HPEM) counter-drone system neutralized 51 airborne drones within seconds after their simultaneous launch. The company’s president claimed it was a world record.

Europe Joins Ukraine-US Talks in Full for First Time Ahead of Berlin Meeting — Europe’s E5 format – comprising Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Poland, along with EU institutions and NATO – joined talks with Ukrainian and US negotiators in full for the first time on Nov. 16, President Volodymyr Zelensky said. The discussion followed Nov. 10-11 Abu Dhabi negotiations with Russia and the US, from which the European side was excluded, as well as a meeting in Moscow between US envoys and Russian

Denmark’s Frederiksen Defends Rwanda Deportation Hub Despite Criticism — Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen on Monday, Nov. 16, defended a plan by Denmark, Austria, the Netherlands, Greece and Germany to set up a deportation center in Rwanda for rejected asylum seekers. French President Emmanuel Macron had criticized the idea of sending migrants to centers outside the EU. Speaking in Vienna, Frederiksen called the project “very modern” and said the current system is “broken.” The center wou

Trump Claims Putin Is ‘Backing Down,’ Would Like to See War End — Speaking to reporters on Monday, Nov. 16, US President Donald Trump said Russian President Vladimir Putin is “backing down” in the war against Ukraine, arguing that the Kremlin could be “a lot more tougher.” Asked about Starlink restrictions, Trump claimed he had not heard about them, despite repeated warnings from Kyiv that a speed cap on the service’s military version, Starshield, is preventing its drone operations. Trump’s rema

EU Sends Ukraine €1.71 Billion for Drones, Air Defense — Ukraine received €1.71 billion ($1.88 billion) from the European Union on Nov. 16 to buy drones, ammunition and air defense systems. Prime Minister Serhiy Koretskyi confirmed that the funds had reached the Treasury account. The payment comes under the EU’s existing Ukraine Support Loan, worth €90 billion ($99 billion), while Kyiv seeks predictable financing for 2027.

Moldova’s Sandu Backs Ukraine’s EU Bid as Von der Leyen Hails ‘Real Prospect’ of Enlargement — Moldovan President Maia Sandu backed Ukraine’s accession bid on Monday, Nov. 16, saying that she would welcome the day both Chișinău and Kyiv become EU members. Her remarks came as the European Commission prepares to close 25 negotiating chapters with Moldova and only seven with Ukraine, due to delays in Kyiv’s judicial and law enforcement reforms. Speaking at the opening of an enlargement forum in Bru

Kellogg: Xi Could Pressure Putin as Russia Leans on China — The former US envoy says Chinese leader Xi Jinping could pressure Putin toward a settlement because Russia is the junior partner in their relationship. Kellogg also backs European participation in negotiations and sees the Oleshky mission as a possible ceasefire model.

More Offensive, Fire Over the Baltic, Ballistics and Ball Bearings — Russian assaults in Donetsk region are suffering record losses as Ukrainian drone units hunt infantry far behind the lines. Ukraine hit Ust-Luga, Russia’s main Baltic oil port, in a complex strike that coincided with the loss of up to three Russian aircraft near St. Petersburg. Starlink problems returned, US-brokered talks went nowhere, NATO failed to down a single stray drone, and a senior Russian air force officer died in a S

Russia’s Oil Revenue Hits Record Since December 2022 — A think tank’s new report suggests that Russia’s oil revenue reached €754 million ($830 million) per day in October – the highest since December 2022, with seaborne crude exports accounting for most of the revenue. Despite the US-Russia diesel deal, the think tank estimated that Russian ports remain strained by Ukrainian strikes, with diesel loadings rising three-fold from September while overall seaborne export volumes dropped 8%.

Zelensky: Over Half of Russian Refinery Capacity Shut Down by Ukrainian Drones — Ukraine’s drone campaign has hit 27 of Russia’s 32 refineries. Zelensky says more than 55% of refining capacity is disabled; Bloomberg estimates nearly 40% offline. Recent attacks hit Azov fuel storage and Ilsky refinery, and shut Volgograd’s plant.

Canada Shuts the Door on Russian Hockey Players — The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) has confirmed that Russia's U20 team will not play at the 2027 World Junior Championship in Canada. Ottawa announced on Nov. 11 that Russian athletes will be denied entry even with valid visas. The ban comes weeks after the Court of Arbitration for Sport ordered Russia's return to international tournaments.

Russian Il-76 Likely Hit in Ukrainian Strike – Report — A Russian Il-76 military transport aircraft was likely hit during Ukraine’s Nov. 10 strike on Staraya Russa airfield, according to aviation monitoring channel AviVector. A satellite image published on Nov. 16 shows apparent damage around an aircraft at the site. Ukraine confirmed attacking the adjoining repair plant, but the extent of damage to the Il-76 remains unclear.

11M Russians ‘Don’t Have a Toilet’, Says Sikorski — Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski accused Russia’s leadership of caring more about territorial conquest than citizens’ living conditions, citing 11 million Russians without a toilet at home. His Sunday post followed reports that Moscow had revived demands to restrict NATO deployments and halt Western military aid to Ukraine. Poland and other European governments have rejected Russian attempts to dictate their security arrangements.

Russia Seeks Seats in UN Telecom Agency — Russia is seeking positions on two influential bodies within the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), a move diplomats say could help Moscow weaken its international isolation over its war against Ukraine. The elections are taking place at the agency’s conference in Doha, where member states are choosing representatives to lead its strategy, budget and radio regulations. Ukraine says Russian strikes, excluding cyberattacks, have caused more than

Ukraine Highlights Media’s Role in Wartime Communication — Ukraine’s officials highlighted the contribution of radio, television and communications workers to the country’s wartime resilience, praising their role in countering Russian disinformation, documenting the consequences of Russia’s invasion and maintaining connections between people. The head of Ukraine’s emergency services said communications specialists continue working even under Russian attacks, helping connect those in need with em

EU Approves Record $8.8 Billion Payment to Ukraine for Reforms — The Council of the EU approved just under €8 billion ($8.8 billion) for Ukraine under the Ukraine Facility – the largest single disbursement yet under the program. Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said he expects the tranche soon, taking Ukraine’s 2026 total under the facility to €13.6 billion ($14.9 billion). The payment, the ninth under the Ukraine Plan, follows Kyiv’s completion of more than 20 reform steps.

Russia Prepares New Strike on Ukraine’s Grid, Air Force Warns — Russia is preparing another attack on Ukraine’s energy facilities and critical infrastructure, Air Force spokesperson Yuriy Ihnat said. Ukraine has received information about the preparations for several days and is awaiting additional air defense ammunition from partners. The warning follows repeated strikes that have damaged power infrastructure, prolonged outages and intensified pressure on repair crews ahead of winter, as Kyiv p

Ukraine Strikes Cut Russian Gasoline Supplies by 31% — Ukraine’s Defense Ministry said drone strikes on Russian oil infrastructure have disrupted nine major refineries, contributing to an around 31% drop in crude processing and worsening fuel shortages across several regions. President Zelensky said more than 55% of Russia’s refining capacity had been knocked offline. Monday’s latest attacks targeted an oil depot and a gas distribution station in Rostov Region.

Kremlin Gets Ready to Sell Russians a ‘Victory’ in Ukraine — The Kremlin has urged ruling-party deputies to prepare for a potential victory and the return of combatants from Ukraine. Earlier reports said Moscow was developing propaganda narratives to portray a possible peace deal as a victory despite heavy losses and limited gains.

Cybersecurity Experts Report 40% Increase in Cyberattacks on Russia in 2026 — The annual domestic cybersecurity threat study by the Moscow-based Positive Technologies independent cybersecurity thinktank published its annual threat study on Monday. It said that successful, reported attacks on Russian organizations rose by 40% year-on-year, from 433 to 605.

Moscow Conscripts Offered Drone Warfare Contracts Instead of Mandatory Service — Moscow is offering conscripts one-year contracts in Russia’s Unmanned Systems Forces instead of mandatory military service, as the Kremlin struggles to meet recruitment targets. Despite promises of lucrative pay and service away from the front, previous recruits have been sent to assault units in Ukraine.

EU Plans €45 Billion Ukraine Loan as 4 States Object — The European Commission plans to propose a new €45 billion loan for Ukraine, backed by the EU budget, the Financial Times reported. It would help cover Kyiv’s estimated €70 billion financing gap in 2027. Czechia, Slovakia, Hungary and Bulgaria oppose further contributions, complicating a proposal that would require agreement from all 27 member states.

600 Ukrainian Drones Targeted Moscow, Shot Down Overnight — Moscow’s mayor claimed that around 600 drones were shot down overnight with most intercepted at long distance from the capital. Russia’s Ministry of Defense said that a total of 1,336 Ukrainian drones were shot down in one of Kyiv's largest aerial attacks of the war.

The Kremlin Is Doubling Down on Its Maximalist Negotiating Strategy — Moscow is digging in with its “non-starter” demands while offering the White House apparent concessions aimed at improving the optics of cooperation with Russia. The strategy hopes to buy time until Western support for Ukraine falters.

Trump, Putin and Xi to Meet Without Set Agenda, Ukraine War Off Table — Trump, Putin, and Xi are expected to meet in China on Thursday without an agreed agenda, with nuclear arms control likely to dominate discussions and Russia’s war against Ukraine largely excluded. The meeting follows disagreements over its format and purpose, with Putin reportedly seeking a new Yalta-style arrangement, while Beijing resists direct involvement in Ukraine peace negotiations.

Russian Strikes Across Ukraine Kill 2, Injure at Least 12 — Russian attacks killed two people and injured at least 12 across Ukraine on Monday, Nov. 16, according to regional authorities. Strikes hit Dnipro and Zaporizhzhia, while Russian drones damaged energy facilities in Cherkasy region and critical infrastructure in the Vinnytsia region and Odesa.

Estonia Prepares to Run Government From Abroad if Russia Invades — Estonia is developing a digital contingency plan to run government services from abroad if Russia invades or occupies its territory. The strategy will use secure cloud systems and overseas data backups to keep essential state functions operating during a crisis.

Prince Harry Makes Surprise Lviv Visit to Back Veterans — Prince Harry made an unannounced weekend visit to Lviv, meeting wounded Ukrainian veterans and attending trials for the 2027 Invictus Games. He also addressed a Superhumans conference on treating war injuries, praised Ukrainian medical teams and expressed confidence in Ukraine’s victory. It was his fourth visit to the country since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022.

Ukraine - NATO Membership for Donbas? — Trump’s reported offer of NATO membership or similar security guarantees in exchange for Ukraine’s withdrawal from Donbas raises serious questions about US commitment and Russia’s intentions. Without firm US backing, such guarantees may be worthless.

NATO Drops Plans for 2027 Leaders’ Summit in Albania Amid Alliance Tensions — NATO is abandoning plans for a 2027 summit in Albania and reducing ministerial meetings amid disagreements over defense spending and broader tensions within the alliance. Albania could host a summit in 2028, while NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte says future gatherings will be organized when necessary.

Estonia to Close All Border Crossings With Russia After GRU-Linked Sabotage Attempt — Estonia will close all border crossings with Russia from Dec. 1 after thwarting an attempted explosion and arson attack on drone manufacturer Threod Systems. Authorities say the GRU recruited the suspects, eight of whom were detained in Latvia. The incident has prompted Moscow to accuse Tallinn of Russophobia and renewed warnings from Estonian officials about Russia’s broader sabotage campaign against European

Crimean Bridge Shut After Ukrainian Strike as Russia Claims Record 1,336 Drones Downed — Ukrainian forces attacked the Crimean Bridge overnight on Nov. 15-16, forcing its closure and delaying four trains traveling to occupied Crimea. Russia’s Defense Ministry claimed its air defenses intercepted and destroyed 1,336 Ukrainian drones across 17 regions, Crimea and the Black and Azov seas. Other reported targets included an oil depot and gas distribution station in Rostov Oblast, an industrial facil

1 Soldier Every 30 Seconds – Nearly 125 Invaders Every Hour — Russia is suffering record casualties, having lost one soldier every 30 seconds on Nov. 9 despite gaining no ground. Moscow accepts the cost because it is fighting for Great Power status and regime survival. Europe – less prepared than Ukraine and watching the US pull back – appears to be an easier target. What next? Is it a case of keep hoping Russia relents, or can we find the courage to stop the Kremlin in Ukraine?

How to End Russia’s War on Ukraine — Efforts to end Russia’s war through negotiations, incentives or Ukrainian concessions misunderstand the nature of the conflict. This war is not about territory but about Vladimir Putin’s goal of restoring Russian control over Ukraine and reshaping Europe’s security order. The reality is that a durable ceasefire will only become possible when Russia is convinced it cannot achieve those aims militarily. The West should therefore focus on reinforcing Ukraine’s s

Ukrainian Drone Blitz Sets Russian Oil Facilities Ablaze Across Three Regions — Ukrainian drones hit an oil depot and a gas distribution station in the Russian city of Azov, Rostov Oblast, overnight on Nov. 16, causing fires at both facilities and injuring three men. Drones also targeted industrial sites in Krasnodar Krai and Yaroslavl Oblast, as Ukraine continues its campaign against Russian energy infrastructure.

Estonia Foils GRU-Ordered Sabotage Attack on Drone Maker Threod Systems — Estonian security authorities thwarted an attempted explosion and arson attack against Estonian drone manufacturer Threod Systems on Saturday, Nov. 14, detaining suspects recruited from Russia, the Internal Security Service (KAPO) and Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna announced. Tsahkna attributed the sabotage plot directly to Russia’s GRU military intelligence agency, stating that battlefield setbacks in Ukraine have driven

EU Naval Forces Intercept Suspected Russian Tanker in Mediterranean — EU naval forces under Operation IRINI boarded a suspected Russian shadow fleet oil tanker in the Mediterranean Sea on Friday, Nov. 13, confirming the vessel was sailing under a false flag, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas announced on Sunday, Nov. 15. Kallas stated that the EU will continue disrupting Russia’s shadow fleet both at sea and diplomatically, noting that EU foreign ministers are expected to approve new sanctions

Romanian PM Condemns Drone Strikes on 3 Commercial Ships Off Danube Delta — Romanian Prime Minister Luca Niculescu condemned a Saturday evening, Nov. 14 drone attack that struck three commercial vessels near the Danube Delta off Sulina, announcing on Sunday that Romanian Air Force fighter jets scrambled twice after defense radars detected aerial targets in the area. Calling the strikes an unacceptable violation of international law caused by Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine, Niculescu pledge

Ukraine Must Introduce Itself — If Kyiv informs the Global South of its place in the world, Ukraine will reverse 30 years of missed opportunities, which have led to large parts of the world either ignorant of or indifferent to Ukraine’s plight.

Biden Blocked Pre-Inauguration Trump Team Talks With Putin, Memoir Says — Former US President Joe Biden reveals in his upcoming memoir “Promise Me, America” that he refused a request from Donald Trump’s transition team to authorize direct negotiations with Russian President Vladimir Putin prior to Trump’s inauguration. Biden was unwilling to allow a “de facto capitulation at Ukraine’s expense,” The Wall Street Journal reported. In excerpts ahead of the Nov. 17 release, Biden also describes Volod

Ukraine Negotiations: Reshuffling the Deck in Europe? — Commentators across the Czech Republic, Poland, Austria, Romania, and Russia analyzed the aftermath of the Abu Dhabi peace talks and the Dublin European Political Community summit. Hospodářské noviny and Rzeczpospolita warned that Russia’s push for a comprehensive European security pact aims to split NATO and revive a “new Yalta,” while Der Standard pointed to European Council President António Costa as the EU’s treaty-mandated representati

In the ‘Kill Zone’, Ukraine Bets on Flying Evacuation Drones — Ukrainian defense manufacturer Skyfall has developed the “Stargate” carbon-fiber aerial medical evacuation drone to rescue wounded soldiers from frontline “kill zones” inaccessible to medics and ground robots. Capable of flying at 105 km/h with a 150-kilogram payload over a 30-kilometer range, the $50,000 craft uses onboard artificial intelligence to maintain stability during Russian electronic warfare jamming.

Ukraine Hits Akhtubinsk Airfield and Tsymbulova Drone Base in Russia — The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine confirmed on Sunday, Nov. 15, that Ukrainian forces struck the Akhtubinsk military airfield in Russia’s Astrakhan region and the Tsymbulova strike drone launch base in the Oryol region overnight. At Akhtubinsk – located 650 kilometers from the front line and housing Russia’s 929th State Flight Test Center and Su-34 bombers – the strike triggered secondary detonations at a guide

UK Rejects Russian Demands on European Security, Nuclear Deterrent — British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has rejected Russian demands to negotiate Europe’s security architecture or restrict allied defense arrangements following talks with European leaders in Dublin, affirming that continental security is for Europe alone to decide as the UK commits its submarine-based nuclear deterrent to NATO. Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha mocked Vladimir Putin’s “Yalta 1945” ambitions given over 1.6

Zelensky: Russia Launched Over 2,300 Drones, 15 Missiles in Week — President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Sunday, Nov. 15, that Russian forces launched more than 2,300 strike drones, 1,590 guided aerial bombs, and 15 missiles against Ukraine over the past week, striking energy and railway infrastructure across multiple regions and injuring 16 people. Zelensky warned that ongoing 161 km/h (100 mph) speed limits on Starshield satellite terminals along the front line and occupied areas prevent U

Reducing Ukraine Aid Sets Scene for More War: Macron — French President Emmanuel Macron warned on Saturday, Nov. 14, that governments seeking to limit aid to Ukraine want to impose an “unjust peace” on Kyiv and Europe, calling it “a recipe for another war.” Macron stated that Vladimir Putin is not negotiating in good faith while stepping up winter strikes on civilians and power grids, urging allies to sustain financial and air defense support and define expectations for US security commitments.
Why the urgency for Europe to seize CBR assets? — It’s not just the moral argument, but financial and strategic imperatives.

Ukraine Blames Russian Hybrid Ops for Vandalism on Warsaw Monuments — Unidentified individuals spray-painted “Slava UPA” in red paint on two Warsaw monuments – including the Monument to the Ghetto Heroes outside the POLIN Museum – among 13 monuments vandalized across Poland over the past week. Local outlets noted that Telegram channels offered $500 for the graffiti, prompting the Ukrainian Embassy in Warsaw to condemn the act as a Russian hybrid warfare provocation aimed at sowing enmity between

Ukraine Strikes Multiple Russian Defense, Petrochemical Plants in Tatarstan, Bryansk — The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine announced on Sunday, Nov. 15, that Ukrainian forces struck three Russian military-industrial and petrochemical enterprises overnight. These include the Nizhnekamskneftekhim synthetic rubber complex and the sole primary distillation unit at the TAIF-NK oil refinery in Tatarstan, over 1,000 kilometers from the border, as well as the Monolit aircraft and helicopter

Svitolina Beats Noskova to Reach WTA Finals Title Match — Ukrainian tennis player Elina Svitolina defeated Czech opponent Linda Nosková in straight sets, 6-2, 6-1, in just over an hour on Nov. 14 to reach the WTA Finals championship match against Russian player Mirra Andreeva, who beat Jessica Pegula. Svitolina reached the semifinals after defeating Aryna Sabalenka 6-3, 3-6, 6-1 in the group stage, snapping a five-match losing streak against the Belarusian.

Pentagon Weighs Smaller 5,000-Troop Cut in Europe, Eyes Eastern Flank — The Pentagon is considering a scaled-back reduction of roughly 5,000 US troops in Europe out of its 80,000-strong force, well below the 25,000 drawdown initially feared by NATO allies. Most reductions are expected to affect Germany amid tensions between German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and US President Donald Trump, while NATO’s eastern flank could see reinforcements ahead of Secretary of War Pete Hegseth’s Dec. 1 recommenda

Drones Strike Akhtubinsk Military Airfield in Russia’s Astrakhan Region — Long-range strike drones reportedly hit the Akhtubinsk military airfield in Russia’s Astrakhan region overnight into Sunday, Nov. 15, triggering at least 30 explosions, a blaze, and apparent secondary ammunition detonations at aircraft parking aprons and depots, OSINT channel Exilenova+ reported. While Ukraine’s General Staff did not immediately comment, Astrakhan Governor Igor Babushkin claimed 31 drones were downed in th

Russian Drone Strikes Residential Building in Kropyvnytskyi, Injuring 3 — A Russian strike drone hit a residential building in the central city of Kropyvnytskyi on Sunday, Nov. 15, injuring three civilians, Kirovohrad Regional State Administration Head Andrii Raikovych reported. One injured man was hospitalized while two others declined inpatient treatment as emergency crews assessed structural damage.

Russian Strike on Chornomorsk Injures 6, Damages Energy Grid — Six people were injured in an overnight Russian strike on the Black Sea port city of Chornomorsk in Odesa region on Sunday, Nov. 15, the State Emergency Service of Ukraine (DSNS) reported. The attack damaged energy infrastructure, heavily destroyed a four-story administrative building, ruptured a gas pipeline, ignited two parked cars, and damaged residential facades and windows.

Kyiv Post: Five Years of Achievements. One Great Mission — Why, as the owner of Kyiv Post, I am proud of how the publication continues to fulfill my father’s vision, and I remain committed to supporting it.

Marko Halanevych: ‘My Art Is About Helping My Country Survive and Endure’ — Marko Halanevych, frontman and vocalist of the Ukrainian band DakhaBrakha, is known not only for his music but also for his graphic art, painting, and design. His #DakhaBrakhaArt project comprises nearly 400 works, sold at charity auctions to support Ukraine’s military. Ahead of the band’s major European tour, he speaks about his artistic practice, inspiration, family, and using art to help Ukraine.

Drones Strike Tatarstan Petrochemical Plant, Rostov Grid, Logistics Bridge in Russia — Long-range strike drones hit the Nizhnekamskneftekhim petrochemical complex in Russia’s Republic of Tatarstan overnight into Sunday, Nov. 15, sparking a fire confirmed by Nizhnekamsk Mayor Radmir Belyaev as damage in the industrial zone. Concurrently, OSINT channels reported drone strikes hitting the 220 kV Taganrog-10 electrical substation – which powers Taganrog and the TAGMET metallurgical plant – and damag

Drone Strikes Cargo Ship Bound for Ukraine in Romanian Waters — An unidentified drone attacked the Palau-flagged commercial vessel Larissa 1 inside Romanian territorial waters overnight into Saturday, Nov. 14, while the ship was en route to Ukraine, Digi24 reported. The strike damaged the ship’s cargo crane without causing injuries or a fire on board, prompting an investigation by the Romanian military, Naval Forces, Coast Guard, and Interior Ministry, Defense Minister Ștefan-Radu Oprea announce

Kushner: US Working on Direct Moscow-Europe Contacts Ahead of Next Talks — US special envoy Jared Kushner announced on Saturday, Nov. 14, that Washington is working to establish direct engagement between Moscow and European partners while preparing the agenda for the next round of trilateral peace talks. Kushner emphasized that lasting peace requires credible security guarantees for Ukraine alongside NATO and new de-escalation mechanisms, asserting that US President Donald Trump will support onl

Russian Glide Bombs Strike Zaporizhzhia, Injuring 6 Including Toddler — Russian tactical aviation launched 12 guided aerial bomb (KAB) strikes against Zaporizhzhia on Saturday evening, Nov. 14, wounding six civilians – including a two-year-old child, three women, and two men – Acting Regional Governor Mykhailo Semikin and Defense Council Co-Chair Ivan Fedorov reported. Blast waves shattered windows across several multi-story apartment blocks, damaged dozens of parked cars, and sparked a fire at

Yet Another Russian War Crime — On Nov. 2, Russian glide bombs destroyed a fortified underground school in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia, while residents collected humanitarian aid, killing at least 55. Extra concrete and seven meters of depth were not enough. Building underground remains necessary, but it offers no guarantee of safety. This was a deliberate war crime, and its details belong at the center of any talks with Moscow – not buried in court databases.
